newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Motor racing-Bridgestone arrival heralds tyre war.
newsitem.headline: Motor racing-Bridgestone arrival heralds tyre war.

text.p: Having enjoyed the luxury of a monopoly for most of the last two decades, tyre giants Goodyear face a new challenge this season with the arrival of Japanese rivals Bridgestone in the Formula One arena.

And if pre-season testing is an accurate measure of their potential, Bridgestone intend to make life as difficult as possible for the established Goodyear men by sparking a 'tyre war' on the world's Grand Prix circuits.

The initial tests conducted by world champion Damon Hill of Britain at Suzuka in Japan last November, followed by startling performances from the Stewart and Ligier (now Prost) teams during winter testing in Europe earlier this year, confirmed that the challenge to Goodyear will be a serious one.

Hill clocked a time in his new Arrows team's 'old' 1995-96 specification car that was 1.2 seconds faster than its more up- to-date model had managed at the Japanese Grand Prix a month before. It was a time good enough to have claimed fourth place on the grid.
"It is perfectly obvious that the tyres did the work and that Bridgestone are very serious and very well-prepared about what they are doing," said a delighted Hill afterwards.

If Bridgestone do win a race, it will end Goodyear's long run of dominance which has resulted in them claiming a total of 344 race victories since 1965. This achievement has enabled them to be the tyre-supplier to 24 world champions -- more than all their rivals combined.

The only other major winning tyre-suppliers to have competed in Formula One are Dunlop (83 wins), Michelin (59), Firestone (49) and Pirelli (45). Continental and Englebert also competed briefly and claimed 10 wins and seven respectively.

In the last decade, however, only Pirelli have taken on the might of Goodyear for a brief spell at the end of the 1980's during which they achieved little other than to prove that the American company enjoyed a comfortable superiority.

This time, however, it is expected to be different. "There's been a lot of hype about the performance of the Bridgestone tyres and one would expect a good performance from them," said Goodyear's spokesman Dermot Bambridge. "We are no expecting an easy run."

Goodyear's proven success record has convinced all the leading teams to remain with them as contracted users of their rubber. This means that they will be supplying tyres for world champions Williams, Ferrari, Benetton, McLaren, Jordan, Sauber and Tyrrell.

Bridgestone, in turn, will supply Arrows, Prost, Minardi, Stewart and Lola -- four of which are virtually all-new teams setting out to upset the establishment in more ways than one. Of these five, only Minardi remain relatively unchanged from last season although many behind-the-scenes financial changes are expected to boost their performances and ensure they get the best from their Bridgestone tyres.
The Stewart and Lola teams are new to Formula One this year while both Arrows and Prost are under new ownership and direction.
In pre-season testing, at Estoril, Jerez and Barcelona, it was clear all of them enjoyed the performances of the Bridgestone 'wet' tyres -- clocking lap-times good enough to embarrass their rivals.

"I just hope there are a few wet races this year -- but, then again, I expect Goodyear will get their act together with a bit of competition this time," said Hill. "It is going to be interesting isn't it?"
